title: Barney Carnage 2.0
outcome: unchanged baseline; bounded diagnostic experiment justified
recommendation: Authorize only a reversible 12 MHz per-title diagnostic comparison against 25 MHz, gated on confirming the same active Level 1 scene; accept no runtime change from present evidence.

resource_context.boundary: All matching browser/Codex processes on this host, including unrelated tabs and agents; not isolated game CPU or memory. CPU is cumulative process seconds; hostTotalCpuPercent is host-wide context. Sum of process working sets may count shared pages multiple times and is not unique physical RAM.
resource_context.cpuMethod: Cumulative CPU deltas only for same PID/name at both ends of each wholly-contained sample interval; new/exited/invalid pairs omitted, potentially undercounting. PID reuse with identical name and monotonic CPU cannot be detected.
resource_context.memoryMethod: Sum of sampled process working sets/private bytes; working sets may double-count shared pages; private bytes are committed allocation, not physical RAM.

protocol.input_during_capture: none; same freshly reached Level 1 white field, starting target region and cursor position
protocol.gate: Confirm active scene with timestamped before/after screenshots and visible target motion; stop if menu/pause/scene cannot be matched.
protocol.acceptance: Diagnostic evidence only; compare medians/ranges for clocks, execution/backlog and observed target displacement/events. Require trusted reference and busy scenes/audio/input/saves qualification before promotion.

limits: Only one visual-work frame during existing capture; target motion rate not established
No original/reference pace; 60.15 guest Hz is runtime clock convention, not proven game pace
Shot red burst observed by coordinator after capture; hit/scoring/rules unverified
Busy levels, pause/menu, audio, saves and physical controller unqualified
Broad process CPU/memory includes unrelated applications; no game-only attribution
